shlokas.sanskrit: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । क्रोधामाहारयत्तीव्रं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.1 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tacchrutvā bhāṣitaṃ tasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | krodhāmāhārayattīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt || 7.69.1 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing that speech of the great-souled Shatrughna, he summoned up a fierce anger and cried out, "Stand! Stand!"

shlokas.sanskrit: पाणौ पाणिं विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान्कटकटाय्य च । लवणो रघुशार्दूलमाह्वयामास चासकृत् ।। 7.69.2 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: pāṇau pāṇiṃ viniṣpiṣya dantānkaṭakaṭāyya ca | lavaṇo raghuśārdūlamāhvayāmāsa cāsakṛt || 7.69.2 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Grinding one hand against the other and gnashing his teeth, Lavana challenged the tiger among the descendants of Raghu again and again.

shlokas.sanskrit: तं ब्रुवाणं तथा वाक्यं लवणं घोरदर्शनम् । शत्रुघ्नो देवशत्रुघ्न इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.3 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tathā vākyaṃ lavaṇaṃ ghoradarśanam | śatrughno devaśatrughna idaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.69.3 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: To Lavana of dreadful aspect, who spoke such words, Shatrughna, the slayer of the enemies of the gods, said these words:

shlokas.sanskrit: न शत्रुघ्नस्तथा जातो यथा ऽन्ये निर्जितास्त्वया । तदद्य बाणाभिहतो व्रज त्वं यमसादनम् ।। 7.69.4 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: na śatrughnastathā jāto yathā 'nye nirjitāstvayā | tadadya bāṇābhihato vraja tvaṃ yamasādanam || 7.69.4 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Shatrughna is not born to be like those others whom you have conquered; therefore today, struck down by my arrow, go to the abode of Yama."

shlokas.sanskrit: ऋषयो ऽप्यद्य पापात्मन्मया त्वां निहतं रणे । पश्यन्तु विप्रा विद्वांसस्त्रिदशा इव रावणम् ।। 7.69.5 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ṛṣayo 'pyadya pāpātmanmayā tvāṃ nihataṃ raṇe | paśyantu viprā vidvāṃsastridaśā iva rāvaṇam || 7.69.5 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Let the seers, the learned Brahmins, behold you slain by me in battle today, O wicked-souled one, just as the gods beheld Ravana."

shlokas.sanskrit: त्वयि मद्बाणनिर्दग्धे पतिते ऽद्य निशाचर । पुरे जनपदे चापि क्षेममेव भविष्यति ।। 7.69.6 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tvayi madbāṇanirdagdhe patite 'dya niśācara | pure janapade cāpi kṣemameva bhaviṣyati || 7.69.6 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "When you, O night-roamer, have been consumed by my arrows and have fallen today, there will be safety both in the city and in the countryside."

shlokas.sanskrit: अद्य मद्बाहुनिष्क्रान्तः शरो वज्रनिभाननः । प्रवेक्ष्यते ते हृदयं पद्ममंशुरिवार्कजः ।। 7.69.7 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: adya madbāhuniṣkrāntaḥ śaro vajranibhānanaḥ | pravekṣyate te hṛdayaṃ padmamaṃśurivārkajaḥ || 7.69.7 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: "Today an arrow with a face like the thunderbolt, sped from my arm, shall pierce your heart, as the ray born of the sun pierces the lotus."

shlokas.sanskrit: एवमुक्तो महावृक्षं लवणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः । शत्रुघ्नोरसि चिक्षेप स च तं शतधाच्छिनत् ।। 7.69.8 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: evamukto mahāvṛkṣaṃ lavaṇaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ | śatrughnorasi cikṣepa sa ca taṃ śatadhācchinat || 7.69.8 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Addressed in this way, Lavana, beside himself with rage, hurled a great tree at Shatrughna's chest, but Shatrughna split it into a hundred pieces.

shlokas.sanskrit: तद्दृष्ट्वा विफलं कर्म राक्षसः पुनरेव तु । पादपान्सुबहून्गृह्य शत्रुघ्नायासृजद्बली ।। 7.69.9 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: taddṛṣṭvā viphalaṃ karma rākṣasaḥ punareva tu | pādapānsubahūngṛhya śatrughnāyāsṛjadbalī || 7.69.9 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Seeing that deed rendered fruitless, the mighty Rakshasa once again seized very many trees and flung them at Shatrughna.

shlokas.sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि तेजस्वी वृक्षानापततो बहून् । त्रिभिश्चतुर्भिरेकैकं चिच्छेद नतपर्वभिः ।। 7.69.10 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śatrughnaścāpi tejasvī vṛkṣānāpatato bahūn | tribhiścaturbhirekaikaṃ ciccheda nataparvabhiḥ || 7.69.10 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And the radiant Shatrughna cut down the many trees as they came flying, each one with three or four straight-jointed arrows.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो बाणमयं वर्षं व्यसृजद्राक्षसोरसि । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो विव्यथे न स राक्षसः ।। 7.69.11 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ vyasṛjadrākṣasorasi | śatrughno vīryasampanno vivyathe na sa rākṣasaḥ || 7.69.11 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then Shatrughna, endowed with valor, loosed a rain of arrows upon the Rakshasa's chest, yet that Rakshasa was not shaken.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततः प्रहस्य लवणो वृक्षमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान् । शिरस्यभ्यहनच्छूरं स्रस्ताङ्गः स मुमोह वै ।। 7.69.12 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tataḥ prahasya lavaṇo vṛkṣamudyamya vīryavān | śirasyabhyahanacchūraṃ srastāṅgaḥ sa mumoha vai || 7.69.12 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then the valiant Lavana, laughing, raised up a tree and struck the heroic Shatrughna upon the head, and he, his limbs giving way, fell into a swoon.

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्मिन्निपतिते वीरे हाहाकारो महानभूत् । ऋषीणां देवसङ्घानां गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा ।। 7.69.13 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasminnipatite vīre hāhākāro mahānabhūt | ṛṣīṇāṃ devasaṅghānāṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ tathā || 7.69.13 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: When that hero had fallen, a great cry of lamentation arose among the sages, the hosts of gods, and likewise the Gandharvas and Apsarases.

shlokas.sanskrit: तमवज्ञाय तु हतं शत्रुघ्नं भुवि पातितम् । रक्षो लब्धान्तरमपि न विवेश स्वमालयम् ।। 7.69.14 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tamavajñāya tu hataṃ śatrughnaṃ bhuvi pātitam | rakṣo labdhāntaramapi na viveśa svamālayam || 7.69.14 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: But the demon, contemptuously supposing Shatrughna slain and cast down upon the ground, did not enter his own dwelling, even though he had gained the opportunity to do so.

shlokas.sanskrit: नापि शूलं प्रजग्राह तं दृष्ट्वा भुवि पातितम् । ततो हत इति ज्ञात्वा तान्भक्षान्समुदावहत् ।। 7.69.15 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nāpi śūlaṃ prajagrāha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhuvi pātitam | tato hata iti jñātvā tānbhakṣānsamudāvahat || 7.69.15 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Nor did he take up his trident when he saw him fallen upon the ground; rather, concluding that he was dead, he carried off those creatures meant to be his food.

shlokas.sanskrit: मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसञ्ज्ञस्तु पुनस्तस्थौ धृतायुधः । शत्रुघ्नो वै पुरद्वारि ऋषिभिः सम्प्रपूजितः ।। 7.69.16 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: muhūrtāllabdhasañjñastu punastasthau dhṛtāyudhaḥ | śatrughno vai puradvāri ṛṣibhiḥ samprapūjitaḥ || 7.69.16 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: After a moment Shatrughna regained his senses and once more stood firm with weapon in hand at the city gate, honored by the sages.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो दिव्यममोघं तं जग्राह शरमुत्तमम् । ज्वलन्तं तेजसा घोरं पूरयन्तं दिशो दश ।। 7.69.17 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato divyamamoghaṃ taṃ jagrāha śaramuttamam | jvalantaṃ tejasā ghoraṃ pūrayantaṃ diśo daśa || 7.69.17 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then he took up that supreme, divine, unfailing arrow, blazing terribly with its energy and filling the ten directions.

shlokas.sanskrit: वज्राननं वज्रवेगं मेरुमन्दरसन्निभम् । नतं पर्वसु सर्वेषु संयुगेष्वपराजितम् ।। 7.69.18 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vajrānanaṃ vajravegaṃ merumandarasannibham | nataṃ parvasu sarveṣu saṃyugeṣvaparājitam || 7.69.18 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Its face was like the thunderbolt and its speed like the thunderbolt; it resembled Mount Meru and Mandara, was bent at all its joints, and was unconquered in every battle.

shlokas.sanskrit: असृक्चन्दनदिग्धाङ्गं चारुपत्रं पतत्रिणम् । दानवेन्द्राचलेन्द्राणामसुराणां च दारणम् ।। 7.69.19 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: asṛkcandanadigdhāṅgaṃ cārupatraṃ patatriṇam | dānavendrācalendrāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca dāraṇam || 7.69.19 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Its body was smeared with blood like sandal-paste, it bore beautiful feathers and wings, and it was the render of the lords of the Danavas, the lords of mountains, and the Asuras.

shlokas.sanskrit: तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं युगान्ते समुपस्थिते । दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि परित्रासमुपागमन् ।। 7.69.20 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: taṃ dīptamiva kālāgniṃ yugānte samupasthite | dṛṣṭvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni paritrāsamupāgaman || 7.69.20 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Beholding it blazing like the fire of Time when the end of an age has come, all beings were seized with terror.

shlokas.sanskrit: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं मुनिभिः साप्सरोगणम् । जगद्धि सर्वमस्वस्थं पितामहमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.69.21 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: sadevāsuragandharvaṃ munibhiḥ sāpsarogaṇam | jagaddhi sarvamasvasthaṃ pitāmahamupasthitam || 7.69.21 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Indeed the whole world, together with the gods, the Asuras, and the Gandharvas, along with the sages and the throngs of Apsarases, grew distressed and approached the Grandfather.

shlokas.sanskrit: उवाच देवदेवेशं वरदं प्रपितामहम् । देवानां भयसंमोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.22 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: uvāca devadeveśaṃ varadaṃ prapitāmaham | devānāṃ bhayasaṃmoho lokānāṃ saṅkṣayaṃ prati || 7.69.22 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: It addressed the boon-granting Great-Grandfather, lord of the lords of gods: 'There is a fear and bewilderment among the gods that portends the destruction of the worlds.'

shlokas.sanskrit: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं च न श्रुतं प्रपितामह । देवानां भयसम्मोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.23 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ ca na śrutaṃ prapitāmaha | devānāṃ bhayasammoho lokānāṃ saṅkṣayaṃ prati || 7.69.23 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'Never before, O Great-Grandfather, has such a thing been seen or heard — this fear and bewilderment among the gods that portends the destruction of the worlds.'

shlokas.sanskrit: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः । भयकारणमाचष्ट लोकानामभयङ्करः । उवाच मधुरां वाणीं शृणुध्वं सर्वदेवताः ।। 7.69.24 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ | bhayakāraṇamācaṣṭa lokānāmabhayaṅkaraḥ | uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ sarvadevatāḥ || 7.69.24 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Hearing those words of theirs, Brahma, the Grandfather of the worlds, the bestower of fearlessness upon the worlds, explained the cause of the fear, and spoke these sweet words: 'Listen, all you deities.'

shlokas.sanskrit: वधाय लवणस्याजौ शरः शत्रुघ्नधारितः । तेजसा तस्य सम्मूढाः सर्वे स्मः सुरसत्तमाः ।। 7.69.25 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: vadhāya lavaṇasyājau śaraḥ śatrughnadhāritaḥ | tejasā tasya sammūḍhāḥ sarve smaḥ surasattamāḥ || 7.69.25 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'For the slaying of Lavana in battle, this arrow has been taken up by Shatrughna; by its energy we, the foremost of the gods, are all bewildered.'

shlokas.sanskrit: एष पूर्वस्य देवस्य लोककर्तुः सनातनः । शरस्तेजोमयो वत्सा येन वै भयमागतम् ।। 7.69.26 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: eṣa pūrvasya devasya lokakartuḥ sanātanaḥ | śarastejomayo vatsā yena vai bhayamāgatam || 7.69.26 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'This, my children, is the eternal, energy-filled arrow of the primeval god, the maker of the worlds, by which this fear has come upon you.'

shlokas.sanskrit: एष वै कैटभस्यार्थे मधुनश्च महाशरः । सृष्टो महात्मना तेन वधार्थे दैत्ययोस्तयोः ।। 7.69.27 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: eṣa vai kaiṭabhasyārthe madhunaśca mahāśaraḥ | sṛṣṭo mahātmanā tena vadhārthe daityayostayoḥ || 7.69.27 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'This great arrow was indeed created by that great-souled one for the sake of Kaitabha and Madhu, for the destruction of those two Daityas.'

shlokas.sanskrit: एक एव प्रजानाति विष्णुस्तेजोमयं शरम् । एषा एव तनुः पूर्वा विष्णोस्तस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.69.28 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: eka eva prajānāti viṣṇustejomayaṃ śaram | eṣā eva tanuḥ pūrvā viṣṇostasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.69.28 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'Vishnu alone fully knows this energy-filled arrow, for this very arrow is the former body of that great-souled Vishnu.'

shlokas.sanskrit: इतो गच्छत पश्यध्वं वध्यमानं महात्मना । रामानुजेन वीरेण लवणं राक्षसोत्तमम् ।। 7.69.29 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ito gacchata paśyadhvaṃ vadhyamānaṃ mahātmanā | rāmānujena vīreṇa lavaṇaṃ rākṣasottamam || 7.69.29 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: 'Go forth from here and behold the foremost of Rakshasas, Lavana, being slain by the heroic, great-souled younger brother of Rama.'

shlokas.sanskrit: तस्य ते देवदेवस्य निशम्य वचनं सुराः । आजग्मुर्यत्र युध्येते शत्रुघ्नलवणावुभौ ।। 7.69.30 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tasya te devadevasya niśamya vacanaṃ surāḥ | ājagmuryatra yudhyete śatrughnalavaṇāvubhau || 7.69.30 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having heard the words of that god of gods, the deities went to where the two, Shatrughna and Lavana, were fighting.

shlokas.sanskrit: तं शरं दिव्यसङ्काशं शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम् । ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम् ।। 7.69.31 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: taṃ śaraṃ divyasaṅkāśaṃ śatrughnakaradhāritam | dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni yugāntāgnimivotthitam || 7.69.31 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: All beings beheld that arrow, resembling something divine and held in Shatrughna's hand, risen up like the fire at the end of an age.

shlokas.sanskrit: अकाशमावृतं दृष्ट्वा देवैर्हि रघुनन्दनः । सिंहनादं भृशं कृत्वा ददर्श लक्षणं पुनः ।। 7.69.32 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: akāśamāvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devairhi raghunandanaḥ | siṃhanādaṃ bhṛśaṃ kṛtvā dadarśa lakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ || 7.69.32 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Seeing the sky thronged with gods, Raghava raised a mighty lion's roar, and then once more set eyes upon the mark before him.

shlokas.sanskrit: आहूतश्च पुनस्तेन शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना । लवणः क्रोधसंयुक्तो युद्धाय समुपस्थितः ।। 7.69.33 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: āhūtaśca punastena śatrughnena mahātmanā | lavaṇaḥ krodhasaṃyukto yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ || 7.69.33 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Summoned again by the great-souled Shatrughna, Lavana, filled with wrath, took his stand for battle.

shlokas.sanskrit: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ तद्धनुर्धन्विनां वरः । तं मुमोच महाबाणं लवणस्य महोरसि ।। 7.69.34 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ākarṇātsa vikṛṣyātha taddhanurdhanvināṃ varaḥ | taṃ mumoca mahābāṇaṃ lavaṇasya mahorasi || 7.69.34 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then that best of bowmen drew the bow back to his ear and loosed the great arrow into Lavana's broad chest.

shlokas.sanskrit: उरस्तस्य विदार्याशु प्रविवेश रसातलम् ।। 7.69.35 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: urastasya vidāryāśu praviveśa rasātalam || 7.69.35 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having swiftly cloven open his chest, the arrow plunged down into the nether world.

shlokas.sanskrit: गत्वा रसातलं दिव्यः शरो विबुधपूजितः । पुनरेवागमत्तूर्णमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् ।। 7.69.36 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: gatvā rasātalaṃ divyaḥ śaro vibudhapūjitaḥ | punarevāgamattūrṇamikṣvākukulanandanam || 7.69.36 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having gone to the nether world, that divine arrow, honored by the gods, came back at once and swiftly to the delight of the Ikshvaku line.

shlokas.sanskrit: शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो लवणः स निशाचरः । पपात सहसा भूमौ वज्राहत इवाचलः ।। 7.69.37 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: śatrughnaśaranirbhinno lavaṇaḥ sa niśācaraḥ | papāta sahasā bhūmau vajrāhata ivācalaḥ || 7.69.37 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Pierced through by Shatrughna's arrow, that night-roaming rakshasa Lavana fell suddenly to the earth like a mountain struck by the thunderbolt.

shlokas.sanskrit: तच्च शूलं महत्तेन हते लवणराक्षसे । पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां रुद्रस्य वशमन्वगात् ।। 7.69.38 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tacca śūlaṃ mahattena hate lavaṇarākṣase | paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ rudrasya vaśamanvagāt || 7.69.38 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: And when the rakshasa Lavana had been slain by him, that great trident, in the sight of all the gods, passed back into the possession of Rudra.

shlokas.sanskrit: एकेषुपातेन भृशं निपात्य लोकत्रयस्यापि रघुप्रवीरः । विनिर्बभावुत्तमचापबाणस्तमः प्रणुद्येव सहस्ररश्मिः ।। 7.69.39 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ekeṣupātena bhṛśaṃ nipātya lokatrayasyāpi raghupravīraḥ | vinirbabhāvuttamacāpabāṇastamaḥ praṇudyeva sahasraraśmiḥ || 7.69.39 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Having utterly struck down with a single shot of his arrow the one who menaced even the three worlds, that foremost hero of the Raghus shone forth with his excellent bow and arrow, like the thousand-rayed sun dispelling the darkness.

shlokas.sanskrit: ततो हि देवा ऋषिपन्नगाश्च प्रपूजिरे ह्यप्सरसश्च सर्वाः । दिष्ट्या जयो दाशरथेरवाप्तस्त्यक्त्वा भयं सर्प इव प्रशान्तः ।। 7.69.40 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: tato hi devā ṛṣipannagāśca prapūjire hyapsarasaśca sarvāḥ | diṣṭyā jayo dāśaratheravāptastyaktvā bhayaṃ sarpa iva praśāntaḥ || 7.69.40 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Then indeed the gods, the sages, and the serpents, and all the apsarases too, paid him honor: 'By good fortune the son of Dasharatha has won the victory!' — and, casting off their fear, they grew calm like a snake at peace.

shlokas.sanskrit: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 69 ।।
shlokas.transliteration: ityārṣe śrīmadrāmāyaṇe vālmīkīye ādikāvye śrīmaduttarakāṇḍe ekonasaptatitamaḥ sargaḥ || 69 ||
shlokas.wordByWord: Thus, in the sacred and glorious Ramayana, the first poem composed by Valmiki, in the glorious Uttara Kanda, ends the sixty-ninth sarga.
